title: French Algiers
capsule: French forces landed at Sidi Ferruch on 14 June 1830 and entered the city of Algiers on 5 July 1830, ending the Ottoman Regency of Algiers. The initial justification was a diplomatic insult by Dey Hussein to the French consul, but the expedition also served domestic political purposes for Charles X. The early years (1830–1834) were characterized by debate in Paris over whether to retain the conquest; by 1834 France formally established a military colony under a governor-general, transitioning from an occupation zone to a structured colonial administration that would endure until 1962.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of French control in the early 1830–1842 period was extremely limited — essentially the city of Algiers and a narrow coastal strip — as the interior remained contested; border delineation for this early phase is approximate.
